minutes.headline: Task force reviewed a streetlight LED design RFP and learned the Select Board will convert it into a standing committee.
minutes.summary: The Green Community Task Force approved prior minutes, reviewed progress on its competitive grant projects, and spent most of the meeting on how to procure a designer for the street light LED conversion after the town buys the lights from Unitil. Members favored a request for proposals for the designer and low-bid for the installer, and debated inspection minimums, GIS data and grant timing. They also discussed a Select Board plan to turn the task force into a standing committee with staggered terms, and agreed to push back on the timing and ask for alternate members.

budget_items.topic: Primary school domestic hot water project overrun
budget_items.what_was_said: The project came in slightly over its grant allocation, offset by savings on the Turkey Hill appliances; a transfer between projects would need approval from the state contacts.
Members agreed to ask the state grant contacts by Friday what it would take to transfer between the appliance and hot water projects.

budget_items.topic: Street light purchase timing and grant
budget_items.what_was_said: An agreement in principle with Unitil is enough to apply for the grant, and the purchase money can carry over.
A member said buying the lights would save the town maintenance costs compared with Unitil.
Members noted installation costs seen elsewhere per light and considered adding lights at intersections for safety.

budget_items.topic: Funding the designer before a grant
budget_items.what_was_said: Members worried the town cannot award a design contract without an appropriation, and the grant may cover design and installation.
Members discussed buying insulation through a Granger or Home Depot account versus a Lowe's bulk discount.

transfers.description: Possible transfer between the Turkey Hill appliance project and the primary school domestic hot water project

decisions.decision: Reach out to the state grant contacts by Friday to ask what a transfer between the appliance and hot water projects would require.
Consensus to use a request for proposals for the LED designer and a low-bid invitation for bids for the installer.
Members leaned toward more than one field inspection, but did not settle a minimum; left for further review of the draft.
Members to send questions for the town of Ayer and for the state contact; chair to consolidate.
Chair to invite the state contact to attend a June meeting and schedule it away from Tuesday and Thursday nights.
Town manager will propose alternate or associate members in the standing committee charge at the next Select Board meeting.

what_happened.line: The task force reached a consensus to use a request for proposals to hire the street light LED designer and a low-bid invitation for bids for the installer.
Members leaned toward requiring more than one field inspection in the design work but did not settle a minimum, leaving it for review of the draft.
The Select Board plans to convert the task force into a standing committee; the town manager will propose alternate or associate members at the next Select Board meeting.
Members will ask the state grant contacts by Friday what a transfer between the appliance and hot water projects would require, after the school hot water project ran slightly over its allocation.
No votes were recorded beyond routine business; the task force heard that an agreement in principle with Unitil is enough to apply for the street light grant.

why_it_matters: The town is preparing to buy its street lights from Unitil and convert them to LEDs, and how the designer and installer are hired will shape the cost and timing of that project.
Members raised that a design contract cannot be awarded without an appropriation, so residents may be asked to vote on funding for the design before any grant is confirmed.
Turning the task force into a standing committee with staggered terms changes who oversees the town's energy grants and projects over time.
